ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is the point charge +q, the middle point is labeled P, and the right-side point is labeled M; the three are on the same straight line. The distances marked in the figure show that the distance from +q to P is a, and the distance from P to M is also a, therefore the distance from +q to M is 2a. Reasoning: If infinity is taken as the zero potential-energy reference, the electric potential of the point charge +q at distance r is V = q/(4πϵ0 r). So V_inf(P) = q/(4πϵ0 a), V_inf(M) = q/(4πϵ0·2a) = q/(8πϵ0 a). Now stipulating that the electric potential at point P is zero is equivalent to subtracting V_inf(P) from all electric potentials, therefore the new electric potential at point M is V_M = V_inf(M) - V_inf(P) = q/(8πϵ0 a) - q/(4πϵ0 a) = -q/(8πϵ0 a).

method.method_draft: First describe the image: +q, P, and M are collinear, with the marked distances +q-to-P = a and P-to-M = a, so +q-to-M = 2a. From the text, set the potential at P as the zero reference. Compute the ordinary point-charge potentials V_inf(P)=q/(4πϵ0 a) and V_inf(M)=q/(4πϵ0·2a). Then use the new reference V_new(M)=V_inf(M)-V_inf(P)=q/(8πϵ0 a)-q/(4πϵ0 a)=-q/(8πϵ0 a).
